A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-ESIM work, and their main text, equations, figures, and tables are readable and matchable. However, both reference appendices that are absent from the supplied files, limiting comparison of supplemental analyses and implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original GEN2 and Eiger noise-calibration measurements and downstream interpolation and deblurring experiments in Section 6, Figures 4–6, and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 reports original sensor-calibration and downstream experiments, including revised interpolation results and a new 200-run parameter-stability analysis in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The APS polynomial calibration, inverse-Q EVS calibration, and joint simulation procedures remain substantively unchanged. Section 5 corrects parameter indices and the correlation sign to agree with Equation 12 already present in v1; this does not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: The sensors, tasks, and named datasets remain the same. Figure 6 changes the demonstrated evaluation scenarios from deformable fish motion to moving color-chart and extremely fast racket/shuttlecock motion, providing limited new qualitative scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The numerical comparisons retain TimeLens, CBMNet, TimeLens-XL, and HR-INR for interpolation, and eSL, MAER, and EFNet for deblurring. Additional H-ESIM fine-tuning of TimeLens-XL is a proposed-method configuration, while the new ESIM/v2e labels identify training sources rather than new comparator methods.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 replaces the no-reference-only interpolation assessment with a skip-one-frame protocol using the withheld APS frame and PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. TimeLens-XL is additionally fine-tuned with H-ESIM, whereas v1 fine-tuned only HR-INR for interpolation. The deblurring protocol remains substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a focused analysis of EVS fitting stability across random initializations. The supplied v2 omits v1's Eiger variance-fit panel and event-probability histogram analysis, while revised Figure 6 supplies new artifact and fast-motion failure examples.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 200 independent randomly initialized calibration runs, parameter boxplots, and coefficients of variation, with reported mean 0.041 and maximum 0.066. v1 has no corresponding repeated-fit analysis. This concerns optimization stability, not uncertainty across downstream training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the original no-reference interpolation scores with reference-based results and adds fine-tuned TimeLens-XL entries. For example, v2 reports Eiger HR-INR PSNR of 32.4129 without and 35.2425 with fine-tuning; these are new-protocol results, not a same-setting improvement over v1. Figure 7 adds stability results. All numerical deblurring scores in Table 2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same substantive noise decomposition, Q-function derivation, and calibration relationships. Explicit time indices, clearer fractions, and explanations of approximation regimes refine the presentation without introducing a new proof or substantively different mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified hybrid-sensor noise model, quantitative calibration, joint RAW/event simulation, and transfer to real downstream tasks. Introductory wording is moderated, but the principal contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 describes the polynomial variance fit as empirical and acknowledges that PRNU is not separately identified. It explains Gaussian-approximation limits, rolling-shutter reference distortion, and fast-motion failures involving event sparsity. It also adds a stability interpretation and drops the earlier histogram-based binomial-support and BRISQUE-domain arguments.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the 1296 × 1024 resolution of the existing 3200-fps input videos, identifies downstream training-data sources, and notes official training-code availability for TimeLens-XL and HR-INR. Section 5 also corrects the documented EVS parameter mapping. The project link and implementation framework remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting noise modeling and approximation assumptions, plus SSIM and LPIPS, while dropping the NRQM reference and MATLAB textbook citation. It softens some criticism of prior work and adds an explicit generic-simulator comparison discussion, retaining the central positioning around jointly calibrated APS–EVS simulation.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work paragraphs are extensively rewritten, technical explanations are revised throughout, and Section 6.2 is reorganized around quantitative interpolation, qualitative interpolation, spatial analysis, and generic-simulator comparisons. An acknowledgements paragraph is also added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 moves, Figure 4 merges distributions and removes a panel, Figure 5 is reorganized, Figure 6 is replaced, and Figure 7 is added. Table 1 is restructured with methods as columns, and Table 2 gains a training-source column.

improvement.justification: The skip-one-frame evaluation provides a more direct reconstruction check than v1's no-reference-only interpolation assessment. The stability experiment and explicit modeling and reference-frame limitations also improve transparency. These gains are moderated by rolling-shutter-distorted references, removal of some calibration diagnostics, and unavailable referenced appendices. The core method and deblurring evidence remain unchanged.
